### 🟢 Approval recommended No active review issues were identified for the DevTools targeting-argument change. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Fixes #1231 by adding `UiTargetArgs` to sandbox launch results when DevTools is `on` or `headless`. Scripts can then use the same targeting arguments as ordinary sandbox launches, such as `--on sandbox -a 4212`. **Changes:** - Populates `UiTargetArgs` using the guest application’s process ID. - Shares argument formatting between ordinary and DevTools launch paths. - Adds a unit test for the DevTools result’s process ID and targeting arguments. The PR reports successful compilation, but unit tests and end-to-end sandbox launches were not run. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/​winapp-CLI/​WinApp.Cli/​Commands/​RunCommand.TargetDevTools.cs` | Creates DevTools results with guest process targeting arguments. | | `src/​winapp-CLI/​WinApp.Cli/​Commands/​RunCommand.Target.cs` | Extracts shared `UiTargetArgs` formatting. | | `src/​winapp-CLI/​WinApp.Cli.Tests/​SandboxRunTests.cs` | Tests targeting arguments for a sandbox DevTools result. |
Review effort: Balanced

comments.body: Closing: main already includes the same change (#1294, include UiTargetArgs in Sandbox DevTools run results), so this PR is superseded. Thanks!
